title: Google AI data center project investigated after 420 football fields of Finnish forest demolished
content: Google’s latest data center construction project in Finland is being investigated after the company representing the search giant reportedly cleared over 300 hectares of forest before obtaining a mandatory environmental impact assessment.

title: Amazon warns $68 billion in blocked data centers threatens US AI lead
content: AWS CEO warns that growing opposition to data centers could undermine U.S. AI leadership, while defending buildouts against concerns over water consumption, electricity costs, pollution, and community impact.

title: Russian firm completes country's first 130nm-capable chipmaking tool, trails modern equipment by 25 years
content: ZNTC completes development of Russia's first 130nm-capable lithography stepper, which could be used to produce chips sometimes late this decade, or rather early next.

title: US Senate kills bill that could potentially shield Americans from skyrocketing power bills due to AI data centers
content: The U.S. Senate has blocked the Ratepayer Protection Act in a 57-43 vote, killing legislation that would have pushed regulators to consider making data centers pay the incremental grid costs created by their massive electricity demand.

title: Customer sends two-stick $16,000 DDR5 memory kit to repair shop
content: A YouTube channel best known for its skillful graphics card fixes has published its first DDR5 module repair video after the economics of RAM repair change.

title: Foxconn September revenue tops NT$1 trillion for first time on AI, ICT demand
content: Driven by strong momentum in AI and consumer electronics, Foxconn reported consolidated revenue of NT$1.158 trillion (US$36.7 billion) for September 2026, marking the first time its monthly revenue has surpassed the NT$1 trillion threshold.

title: Largan Precision sees steady smartphone lens demand as CPO fibre arrays near production
content: Largan Precision reported September consolidated revenue of NT$5.78 billion (US$181.99 million), up 15% from August but down 7% from a year earlier. Third-quarter revenue rose 15% sequentially to NT$15.65 billion.

title: Pegatron AI servers boost September revenue
content: Pegatron's AI server business is ramping up in 2026, with co-CEO Kuang-Chih Cheng recently saying new orders from a US client have begun shipping and are expected to lift September revenue. He added that the company still sees AI server revenue growing by triple digits next year, with the business potentially accounting for 10% of sales.

title: Kyushu's chip expo expands as Japan adds a chip design focus
content: Japan's Kyushu Semiconductor Industry Exhibition, known as K-Semi, grew 36% at this year's edition in Fukuoka, held from September 30 to October 1, 2026, as chip makers expanded their presence in Kyushu. The event also added a semiconductor design zone for the first time and was held alongside the debut Kyushu Next-Generation Energy Exhibition, or K-Ene.

title: Southern Taiwan Science Park revenue climbs 36.5% in first eight months of 2026
content: Companies in the Southern Taiwan Science Park (STSP) posted record revenue of NT$2.495124 trillion (US$78.59 billion) in the first eight months of 2026, up 36.5% from a year earlier, according to the STSP Bureau. The bureau said the growth reflected the global AI boom and the park's expanding role in the high-tech supply chain.

title: AMD's Lisa Su back in Taiwan as AI capacity crunch spreads beyond TSMC
content: AMD CEO Lisa Su arrived in Taiwan on October 5 for a lightning visit, less than five months after her May trip. No major public events are scheduled, but meetings with key suppliers are planned. Industry sources said her core mission was to meet TSMC and, more importantly, to coordinate capacity with packaging, testing, and substrate suppliers that are facing tight supply and rising prices.

title: CHPT posts record quarterly revenue as chip test demand rises
content: Chunghwa Precision Test Tech (CHPT), a supplier of semiconductor test interfaces, posted record revenue for September and the third quarter of 2026 as demand for AI-related chip testing kept capacity utilization high. Revenue for the first nine months of the year also reached a record.

title: Taiwan teams accelerate 2D semiconductor transfer with published research in Nature
content: Researchers in Taiwan are intensifying efforts to turn 2D semiconductor materials from basic science into practical applications, with a series of studies published in Nature. The latest work, published in the October 1 issue of the leading scientific journal, follows another Nature paper published on July 1, 2026, underscoring the push in Taiwan's academia to speed up research in next-generation semiconductors.

title: Huawei counters chip-node limits with Ascend, SuperPoD and τ law
content: Huawei is increasingly framing its semiconductor strategy around a simple constraint: if advanced process nodes remain limited, more performance must come from architecture, interconnect and system-level efficiency.

title: China's ASML DUV stockpile spurs calls to close export-control loophole
content: Chinese semiconductor manufacturers have stockpiled hundreds of immersion deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography systems worth billions of dollars in recent years, prompting a Washington think tank to call for tighter export controls on equipment that could still support advanced chip production.

title: Cheap SiC substrates ignite demand wave, reshape ecosystem
content: Prices for low-cost 6-inch silicon carbide (SiC) substrates, after years of capacity expansion and brutal price wars, are now showing clear signs of bottoming out in the second half of 2026. The cheap material has also unleashed wave after wave of demand, with China's domestic stimulus tightening SiC wafer fabrication capacity and spilling over into Taiwan's supply chain.

title: AI hardware is propping up world trade, and pulling it toward East Asia and North America
content: The resilience of global goods trade amid tariff escalation and an energy shock is real, but it rests on a narrow base. A breakdown of ITC Trade Map export data shows that a handful of AI hardware categories, led by servers, processors and memory chips, account for well over a third of the growth in world exports, and that the gains are flowing overwhelmingly to a small group of East Asian exporters and their North American customers.
